workflows.name: Vendor Media Campaign Briefing & Creative Development

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-count of "Account Manager conducts campaign briefing with vendor" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review for BuildRight brand guidelines compliance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-generate of "Production and distribution" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-386 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Advertising Campaign Execution (PA-48.2).)
- operational: Account Manager review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Brand-infringement risk**: vendor-supplied creative violates BuildRight brand guidelines or implies unintended endorsement; mitigated by the creative review gate checking every vendor-provided asset for guideline compliance (step 2)

- **Scope-ambiguity risk**: campaigns built without defined objectives/audience/KPIs produce off-target creative and later disputes; mitigated by the structured campaign briefing (objectives, target audience, success metrics) at kickoff (step 1)
System Touchpoints: - Campaign brief management with creative workflow (W2006.2)
- Integration with W14.1 (campaign planning) for promotional calendar alignment
Time Estimate: - 30–60 min briefing; 3–5 days creative; 3–5 days production

steps.activity: Account Manager conducts campaign briefing with vendor: (a) campaign objectives: brand awareness, new product launch, promotional sales lift, (b) target audience: DIY homeowners, trade professionals, specific category buyers, (c) key message and call-to-action, (d) campaign duration and channels, (e) creative assets available from vendor or BuildRight creative needed

Creative development: (a) if vendor provides creative: review for BuildRight brand guidelines compliance, (b) if BuildRight produces: Creative Designer develops per vendor brief (additional production fee), (c) creative specifications: size, resolution, format per media type, (d) vendor approves final creative before production
Production and distribution: (a) print materials: produced and shipped to stores per W2000, (b) digital content: uploaded to CMS or ecommerce platform per W2001/W2003

fields.Participants: Marketing Manager, Visual Merchandiser, Digital Marketing Manager
fields.Trigger: Campaign creative approved and ready for launch

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "check" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-generate of "print catalog/flyer distributed" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-monitor of "monitoring" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-386 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Advertising Campaign Execution (PA-48.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Dead-air risk**: a booked campaign launches with placements missing — stores not installed, ads not serving; mitigated by the launch checklist plus 48-hour post-launch monitoring with immediate issue remediation (steps 2–3)
- **Timing-mismatch risk**: media goes live before the vendor's promotional pricing activates, showing shoppers stale prices; mitigated by coordinated launch timing against price activation (step 1)
System Touchpoints: - Campaign launch management with channel coordination (W2007.1)
- Integration with W13 (promotions) for pricing alignment

steps.activity: Campaign orchestration: (a) simultaneous launch across booked channels: in-store placements, ecommerce ads, digital signage, (b) coordinate timing with vendor's promotional pricing activation per W13, (c) ensure product availability at stores running campaign (ATP check)

Launch checklist: (a) in-store materials installed per W2000, (b) ecommerce ads live and serving, (c) digital signage content playing, (d) print catalog/flyer distributed (if applicable), (e) all placements verified with photo evidence or screenshot

Post-launch monitoring (first 48 hours): (a) check ecommerce ad impressions and clicks, (b) verify in-store installation compliance from store photos, (c) address any issues: creative errors, placement issues, product stockouts at campaign stores

workflows.name: In-Store Campaign Compliance Monitoring & Photo Verification

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-review of "reviews" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "tracked per W67" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalate to Regional Manager" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-386 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Advertising Campaign Execution (PA-48.2).)
- operational: Visual Merchandiser review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Photo-fraud risk**: staged or reused store photos mask non-installation while the vendor pays full rate; mitigated by Visual Merchandiser review of weekly per-placement photos with re-verification on anomalies (step 1)

- **Mid-campaign decay risk**: materials damaged or removed mid-flight silently erode delivered impressions; mitigated by weekly compliance scoring (fully/partially/non-compliant) with 3-day re-installation and the ≥90% compliance-rate target (steps 2–3)
System Touchpoints: - Photo upload and compliance review system (W2008.1)
Time Estimate: - 1–2 hours/week for Visual Merchandiser; 15 min/store/week for Store Manager

steps.activity: Weekly: Visual Merchandiser requests campaign compliance photos from stores: (a) Store Manager photographs each active placement, (b) uploads to campaign management system, (c) Visual Merchandiser reviews: (i) correct placement location, (ii) materials in good condition, (iii) products displayed correctly on endcaps

Compliance scoring: (a) fully compliant: materials installed correctly and in good condition, (b) partially compliant: installed but with issues (wrong location, damaged materials), (c) non-compliant: not installed or removed, (d) store compliance score tracked per W67 (store performance)

Remediation: (a) non-compliant stores: re-ship materials and request re-installation within 3 days, (b) repeated non-compliance: escalate to Regional Manager, (c) compliance rate target: ≥ 90% of stores compliant within first week of campaign

fields.Trigger: Ecommerce ad campaign active; optimization cycle

workflows.name: Ecommerce Campaign Performance Optimization & A/B Testing

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitoring" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-test of "test" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report optimization results to vendor with recommendations for next campaign…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-386 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Advertising Campaign Execution (PA-48.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Burn risk**: underperforming campaigns (CTR <0.5% or ROAS <3x) keep spending unnoticed; mitigated by daily performance flags feeding bid adjustments, creative rotation, and targeting refinement (steps 1–2)

- **False-conclusion risk**: A/B tests read on noise produce durable but wrong optimization lessons; mitigated by structured creative/headline rotation with documented results reported to the vendor monthly (steps 2–3)
System Touchpoints: - Integration with W50 (PIM) for product data and W19 (ecommerce) for sales attribution

steps.activity: Daily monitoring: (a) impressions, clicks, CTR, CPC, spend, conversions (sales attributed to ad), (b) ROAS: revenue from ad clicks ÷ ad spend, (c) flag campaigns with CTR < 0.5% or ROAS < 3x for optimization

Optimization actions: (a) adjust bids: increase CPC for high-performing keywords, decrease for low-performing, (b) A/B test: rotate banner creative, test different headlines, (c) targeting refinement: narrow audience segments for better conversion, (d) budget reallocation: shift spend from underperforming to overperforming placements
Monthly: report optimization results to vendor with recommendations for next campaign cycle

fields.Participants: Account Manager, Marketing Manager, AP Clerk, Vendor
fields.Trigger: Vendor has co-op advertising fund agreement per W513
fields.Volume: ~30–50% of media campaigns funded partly by vendor co-op

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-validate of "checks vendor co-op fund availability" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "records co-op fund utilization per vendor" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-post of "Post-campaign settlement" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-claim risk**: co-op reimbursement claimed beyond the vendor's remaining fund balance or without proof of execution; mitigated by the availability check (agreement budget, YTD spend, balance) and evidence-backed claims (steps 1, 3)

- **Allocation-error risk**: the BuildRight/vendor cost split booked differently from the agreement distorts media P&L and vendor balances; mitigated by per-agreement cost allocation computed at campaign level (step 2)
System Touchpoints: - Campaign cost allocation with co-op split (W2010.2)
- Integration with W513 (vendor co-op advertising) for fund management
Time Estimate: - 15–30 min per campaign for co-op coordination

steps.activity: Account Manager checks vendor co-op fund availability: (a) annual co-op budget per vendor agreement per W513, (b) YTD co-op spend, (c) remaining balance available for current campaign

Campaign cost allocation: (a) total campaign cost: BuildRight media rate + production costs, (b) vendor co-op contribution: per agreement (typically 50–100% of media cost), (c) BuildRight contribution: remaining portion, (d) system records co-op fund utilization per vendor

Post-campaign settlement: (a) AP Clerk processes co-op reimbursement claim to vendor: proof of execution (photos, screenshots), campaign performance summary, (b) vendor reimburses BuildRight per co-op terms, or (c) offset against AP (vendor credit memo)

fields.Frequency: Per campaign completion; monthly vendor reports

workflows.name: Retail Media Campaign Reporting & Vendor Presentation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "System generates campaign performance report" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Account Manager presents report to vendor" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-compile of "compiles retail media network performance for CMO" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-386 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Advertising Campaign Execution (PA-48.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Credibility risk**: impression and sales-lift estimates challenged by vendors stall renewals; mitigated by system-generated reports using pre-vs-during baselines and control-group comparisons with methodology shown (steps 1–2)

- **Churn-blindness risk**: vendor dissatisfaction surfaces only when rebookings stop; mitigated by quarterly CMO reporting on vendor retention, fill rate, and top performers with corrective selling actions (step 3)
System Touchpoints: - Integration with W35 (management reporting) for consolidated media revenue view
Time Estimate: - 30–60 min per vendor presentation; 1 day/quarter consolidated

steps.activity: System generates campaign performance report: (a) in-store: store compliance rate, estimated impressions (foot traffic × placement location), associated product sales lift (pre vs. during campaign), (b) ecommerce: impressions, clicks, CTR, CPC, ROAS, attributed revenue, (c) print: distribution count, redemption rate (if promo code used)

Account Manager presents report to vendor: (a) campaign performance vs. objectives, (b) ROI analysis: vendor investment vs. sales lift, (c) recommendations for next campaign: optimization insights, (d) upsell: suggest additional placements or channels based on performance

Quarterly: Marketing Manager compiles retail media network performance for CMO: (a) total media revenue, (b) fill rate: % of inventory sold, (c) vendor retention: % of vendors rebooking, (d) top-performing placements by revenue and vendor ROI

fields.Participants: Marketing Manager, Account Manager, VP Merchandising, Vendor
fields.Trigger: Seasonal planning cycle (aligned to BuildRight's seasonal calendar)

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "catalog feature page" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-count of "Account Manager sells seasonal packages to vendors" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "tracked as single campaign" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-386 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Advertising Campaign Execution (PA-48.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unsold-inventory risk**: seasonal placements expire worthless when not pre-sold before the window; mitigated by priority pre-selling of seasonal packages to existing media vendors ahead of each season (step 2)

- **Relevance risk**: package content misaligned to the season's demand pattern (summer garden/aircon vs. rainy waterproofing vs. ber-months); mitigated by package design aligned to BuildRight's seasonal calendar (step 1)
System Touchpoints: - Integration with W13 (promotions) for seasonal calendar alignment

steps.activity: Marketing Manager develops seasonal media package: (a) season: summer (garden, outdoor, aircon), rainy (waterproofing, flood control), Ber-months (holiday, home improvement), etc., (b) package components: (i) endcap in all stores for 2 weeks, (ii) homepage banner for 1 week, (iii) catalog feature page, (iv) social media mention, (c) package pricing: 20–30% discount vs. à la carte booking, (d) limited availability: 5–10 packages per season

Account Manager sells seasonal packages to vendors: (a) priority offer to existing media vendors, (b) present seasonal sales opportunity (higher foot traffic during seasonal peaks), (c) close deals before seasonal catalog deadline
Execution: (a) package campaigns launched per W2007 multi-channel orchestration, (b) all package components tracked as single campaign

fields.Participants: Marketing Manager, Visual Merchandiser, Digital Marketing Manager, Vendor
fields.Trigger: Media campaign quality issue or exception

workflows.name: Retail Media Campaign Exception & Quality Issue Resolution

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-detect of "ad not serving, creative error, wrong product linked" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "document all issues for quality improvement tracking" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-386 (ensure controlled execution — Vendor Advertising Campaign Execution (PA-48.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Makegood-inconsistency risk**: vendor compensation for similar failures varies case by case, breeding disputes; mitigated by standard resolution SLAs (in-store 5 days, ecommerce 24 hours, signage 48 hours) with a defined pro-rata credit/extension policy (steps 2–3)
- **Recurrence risk**: exceptions fixed one-off but never trended by channel; mitigated by issue identification capturing in-store/ecommerce/signage failure modes for pattern review (step 1)

steps.activity: Issue identification: (a) in-store: materials not installed, installed incorrectly, damaged, removed prematurely, (b) ecommerce: ad not serving, creative error, wrong product linked, (c) digital signage: screen malfunction, wrong content playing

Resolution: (a) in-store: re-ship and re-install within 5 days, (b) ecommerce: fix within 24 hours, (c) digital signage: fix within 48 hours, (d) for all issues: extend campaign duration to compensate for downtime/issue period

Vendor compensation: (a) if issue caused by BuildRight: credit vendor for affected period (pro-rata refund or campaign extension), (b) if issue caused by vendor (late creative, wrong specs): no compensation, (c) document all issues for quality improvement tracking
